blocks.content: Soil pH measures acidity or alkalinity. Most crops grow best in slightly acidic to neutral soils (pH 6–7.5). Highly acidic soils limit nutrient availability.
Most crops grow best in slightly acidic to neutral soils (pH 6–7.5).

items: Competitive exams frequently ask for the ideal crop soil pH range: 6–7.5 (slightly acidic to neutral).
Remember that high soil acidity negatively impacts fertility by limiting key nutrient availability.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Soil pH is a chemical measure used to determine soil acidity or alkalinity.
The optimal soil condition for most crops is slightly acidic to neutral, spanning a pH of 6 to 7.5.
Highly acidic soil environments directly impair plant growth by restricting essential nutrient availability.
